sections.purpose: To establish a uniform, GLP-compliant procedure for maintaining laboratory logbooks, raw data records, and instrument logs to ensure data integrity, traceability, and readiness for PCI and regulatory inspection.
sections.scope: Applicable to all pharmacy laboratory departments and all personnel generating, recording, or reviewing primary analytical data — including students, research scholars, technicians, and teaching staff.
procedure: Issue a new laboratory logbook through the authorized stationery/store with a unique serial number; record the issue in the logbook register maintained by the Laboratory In-charge.

On the first page of every logbook, fill in: Department name, Subject/Course/Project title, Academic year/Project period, Logbook serial number, Name and designation of the user, and Name of the supervising staff.
Number all pages consecutively before use — pre-numbering prevents insertion or removal of pages.
Record all experimental data directly and immediately in the logbook in permanent blue or black ink — never use pencil.
Record data in real time as the experiment progresses — do not record data on loose paper for later transfer into the logbook.
Record all raw observations first (instrument readings, balance readings, times, temperatures, volumes) — then perform calculations.
Every page entry must include: date, experiment number/name, and the analyst's initials.

For corrections: draw a single horizontal line through the incorrect entry; write the correct value adjacent to it; initial and date the correction. Never use correction fluid, eraser, or write over the original entry.
Leave no blank spaces or lines in the logbook — draw a diagonal line through any unused space before proceeding.
All significant figures must be recorded as observed — do not round off raw data at the point of recording.
Attach or affix all instrument printouts, chromatograms, and spectral data securely to the logbook or cross-reference by page number.
At the end of each practical session or experiment, the supervisor/in-charge signs and dates the completed pages.
Completed logbooks must be submitted to the Laboratory In-charge for review, endorsement, and storage — do not retain completed logbooks with individual users.
Store completed logbooks in a designated, locked, fire-resistant cabinet — retain for a minimum of 5 years or as per institutional policy.
Instrument logbooks (usage, calibration, maintenance records) must be kept with the instrument at all times — these are primary inspection documents.
precautions: Data integrity is a regulatory and ethical obligation — falsification, backdating, or fabrication of records in a laboratory logbook constitutes scientific misconduct and may have legal consequences.
Never tear out pages from the logbook — a missing page is treated as data falsification during inspection.
Never use correction fluid (Wite-Out, Tipex) — obscuring original data is a critical GLP violation.
Never record data in pencil — pencil entries can be erased and constitute a data integrity risk.
Never transfer data from a loose paper scratchpad into the logbook after the experiment — this is backdating and a GLP violation.
Electronic data (from computerized instruments) must be backed up, time-stamped, access-controlled, and audit-trailed — electronic logbooks must meet 21 CFR Part 11 equivalent standards.
Supervisors are responsible for ensuring their students/staff maintain logbooks correctly — logbook quality is assessed during PCI inspections.
